title: Capstone: Order-Ops Server + Consumer
objective: After this lesson you will be able to assemble the complete order-operations MCP server (tools, resources, prompts, gates, audit) with an agent consumer, evaluate tool-calling end to end, and present it as traced runs plus a findings memo — ready for the final assessment and your capstone project.
why: Nine lessons of protocol pieces; one lesson of shipped server. The walkthrough performs the full build once — pinned scaffold, catalog/order tools, policy resource, triage prompt, gated refund, audit logging, consumer loop, gold evaluation — so your project repeats a demonstrated shape with numbers attached. Assembly is the final MCP skill.

blocks.text: Build in dependency order with verification per stage: (1) **scaffold pinned** (SDK/zod/Node/spec versions + Inspector connects); (2) **read tools + resource + prompt** (list/call/read/get green); (3) **gated refund** (elicitation path demonstrated, idempotency proven by re-run); (4) **consumer loop** (route → call → validate → generate with routing tests); (5) **gold evaluation** (selection/validity/safety per segment + one iteration). No stage starts on unverified prior output.

blocks.caption: Manifest-first: pins, server map, safety, consumer, eval gates

blocks.text: Three traced runs (the demo that proves)

Lookup run (SKU path → structuredContent → cited answer, one round trip), gated run ($500 refund → elicitation → edited amount → re-validated → executed → audited), attack run (injection ticket → quarantined pre-tool with logged attempt). Each with trace (JSON-RPC methods + verdicts), state, and timing: capability, governance, and defense demonstrated — not described.

Baseline per segment with weakest named (selection accuracy, arg validity, safe-failure coverage), one iterated fix with delta (sibling descriptions after mis-selections), gate health (approval latency design), audit completeness statement, and deferred list (Streamable HTTP + OAuth next, Tasks extension later). Measured, cited, improvable.

blocks.title: Audit the manifest
blocks.note: Run it: expect four PASS lines then 'manifest sound'. Version pins, gated money, versioned resources, sized gold — architecture audited before a single server starts.

items: Assemble in dependency order with per-stage gates: pins → reads → gated money → consumer → gold eval
Trace one run per kind (lookup/gated/attack) with methods, verdicts, timing
Memo: baselines, iterated delta, gate health, audit statement, deferred list

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the manifest audit and confirm soundness. (b) Break it (drop the @gated suffix) and state the real-world harm the audit now catches. (c) Draft your capstone manifest (same shape, your domain's tools/resources/prompts) with version pins and one gate per destructive tool.
hints: Baseline sound (4 PASS); suffix dropped → money-gated check FAILs — the audit catches ungated money statically.
Harm: autonomous ungated refunds the moment any consumer mis-selects — amounts move without approval or audit.
Your manifest needs pins, per-tool gate flags, versioned resources, sized gold — coverage thinking for builds.
exercise.why: Static money-gate auditing (suffix conventions checked in code review/CI) plus manifest-driven builds make safety structural: the audit catches what enthusiasm misses, before servers start.
exercise.code: // Manifest-audit pattern: pins, gates, versions, gold size as runnable checks.

quiz.q: Assembly order for the MCP server?
options: Pinned scaffold → reads/resource/prompt → Inspector-verified ground → gated money → consumer → gold eval — dependencies first, verified per arrow
quiz.explain: Blast-radius ordering with per-arrow verification: reads prove ground that money requires; eval measures the assembled whole.

quiz.q: Audit flags refund tool without @gated. Meaning?
options: Static safety failure: ungated money tool shippable — fix before starting the server, not after an incident
quiz.explain: Gate flags are machine-checkable safety invariants. Missing gates block builds the way failing tests block merges.

quiz.q: Three traced runs cover lookup/gated/attack. Why these three?
options: Capability (can it work), governance (is money supervised), defense (do attacks fail safe) — the three properties stakeholders fund
quiz.explain: Coverage by property: function, supervision, and safety. Happy-only demos prove none of the three that matter.

summary: Manifest-audited assembly, one traced run per property (capability/governance/defense), findings with per-segment truth. Nine lessons become one operating server — assessment next, capstone after.
next: Course complete: take the 12-question final assessment (70% to pass), then ship the Order-Ops MCP Server capstone — and step into production agents.
